SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is traditional culture important? (1 mark)
   A. It gives identity and teaches values
   B. It stops all change
   C. It makes people fight
   D. It has no use

2. Which food is made of maize and beans mixed together? (1 mark)
   A. Githeri
   B. Mahamri
   C. Chapati
   D. Pilau

3. What is culture? (1 mark)
   A. The way of life of a community
   B. A type of road
   C. A kind of weather
   D. A kind of animal

4. Which words help to tell a history in order? (1 mark)
   A. First, then, later, today
   B. Big, small, tall
   C. Up, down, left
   D. Red, blue, green

5. What is a timeline? (1 mark)
   A. A weather chart
   B. A line showing events in the order they happened
   C. A kind of ruler
   D. A picture of a school

6. Who can tell you about the history of your school? (1 mark)
   A. A random person
   B. A shop
   C. A stranger who has never visited
   D. The headteacher or teachers who have been there long

7. Which of these is a benefit of economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. They give people jobs and income
   B. They close schools
   C. They make people poor
   D. They stop trade

8. Which of these is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Watching clouds
   C. Singing at bedtime
   D. Fishing

9. Why must children not do hard or dangerous work? (1 mark)
   A. It is a school rule
   B. It is fun
   C. It harms their health and schooling
   D. It makes them stronger

10. Where are fish processing factories found? (1 mark)
   A. In a desert without water
   B. In the sky
   C. On the shores of Lake Victoria
   D. On top of Mount Kenya

11. What is an industry? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A kind of farm animal
   C. A type of weather
   D. A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale

12. Which factor makes a place suitable for a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Good roads and nearby workers
   B. No workers
   C. No water
   D. No roads

13. What is an enterprise? (1 mark)
   A. A school rule
   B. A game
   C. A business activity to make goods or provide services
   D. A weather chart

14. What is a cost? (1 mark)
   A. Profit
   B. Salary
   C. Money received
   D. Money spent on the project

15. A group spent Ksh 600 and earned Ksh 500. What happened? (1 mark)
   A. A loss of Ksh 100
   B. A profit of Ksh 100
   C. A profit of Ksh 1,100
   D. No change

16. Which action shows respect? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking desks
   B. Insulting classmates
   C. Ignoring teachers
   D. Greeting teachers politely

17. Which is a good way to develop a quality like punctuality? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Wait for others to do it
   C. Practise it every day
   D. Practise it once a year

18. What should you do if something online makes you feel scared? (1 mark)
   A. Tell a trusted adult
   B. Meet the stranger
   C. Keep it secret
   D. Reply angrily

19. What should you do if you are very angry? (1 mark)
   A. Walk away and calm down
   B. Shout insults
   C. Hit someone
   D. Break something

20. What is forgiveness? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring the wrong
   B. Keeping anger forever
   C. Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   D. Punishing without listening

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept. (3 marks)

22. Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values. (4 marks)

23. Explain how you can stay calm when you feel very angry. (3 marks)

24. Describe how your class could showcase its school enterprise project. (5 marks)

25. A group spent Ksh 900 and earned Ksh 600. Say whether this is a profit or a loss and find the amount. Suggest two reasons why it may have happened. (4 marks)

26. Explain the difference between a right and a duty and give one example of each in school. (4 marks)

27. List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school. (4 marks)

28. Explain why it is important to keep records of income and costs. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It gives identity and teaches values
   Culture helps us to know who we are.

2. A — Githeri
   Githeri is maize and beans.

3. A — The way of life of a community
   Culture is the way of life passed on from generation to generation.

4. A — First, then, later, today
   Time words link events in order.

5. B — A line showing events in the order they happened
   A timeline shows events in order.

6. D — The headteacher or teachers who have been there long
   Reliable people and records give true information.

7. A — They give people jobs and income
   Economic activities provide income and food.

8. D — Fishing
   Fishing produces food and income.

9. C — It harms their health and schooling
   Child labour is harmful and against the law.

10. C — On the shores of Lake Victoria
   Fish are processed near the lake where they are caught.

11. D — A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   Industries change raw materials into products or provide services.

12. A — Good roads and nearby workers
   Transport and workers matter.

13. C — A business activity to make goods or provide services
   Enterprises earn money by making goods or services.

14. D — Money spent on the project
   Costs are expenses.

15. A — A loss of Ksh 100
   They spent more than they earned: 600 - 500 = 100.

16. D — Greeting teachers politely
   Polite greetings show respect.

17. C — Practise it every day
   Habits grow with practice.

18. A — Tell a trusted adult
   A trusted adult can help.

19. A — Walk away and calm down
   Cooling down prevents harm.

20. C — Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   Forgiveness ends quarrels.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk away, take slow deep breaths, and count to ten before speaking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Set up a stall with the goods, display a poster, show records of costs and income, explain each team member's role, and let visitors ask questions and give feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: It is a loss of Ksh 300. Sales may have been low because the price was too high or not enough people knew about the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for loss, 1 mark for the amount 900 - 600 = 300, 1 mark for each reason.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: A right is something you are allowed, such as learning in a safe place. A duty is something you must do, such as following the rules.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each relevant question.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: To know whether there is profit or loss, to show honesty, and to plan better next time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
